solution: Fraction part: the digits after the point stand for $2^{-1}$ and $2^{-2}$, so $.01_2 = 0\cdot\tfrac12 + 1\cdot\tfrac14 = 0.25$.
concept: Positions after the radix point carry negative powers of the base.

common_wrong.why: The digits after the point were copied across. In base 2 they stand for halves and quarters, not hundredths.
The 1 was read as the $2^{-1}$ digit. It is the second digit after the point, so it is worth $2^{-2} = 0.25$.

solution: In base 16 the digit D stands for 13.
concept: Each hexadecimal digit is worth digit × a power of 16.

common_wrong.why: This reads D as 13 but weights the 2 by 8, the octal place value.
The digits were written side by side (2 and 13) instead of being weighted by their places.
